title: Cave sizes: a small one and a big one
question: Is the range right — is the big one big enough, and does the small one still read as worth finding? And see the last paragraph about the vertical banding.
context_md:
Your ask: *"Caves should be bigger or at least the upper limit should be
bigger, then should have a variety of sizes."*

Both of these are canyon, same build, different seeds, same zoom. A is a
small one, B is near the top of the range. Flat lighting so the shape
reads.

The envelope used to be one fixed size — 181 x 71 — for every cave in
every world. It is now drawn per system, heavy-tailed and weighted small,
up to 401 x 161. Over 16 seeds x 5 presets:

|                     | before | now |
|---|---|---|
| span across         | always 181 | median 73-157, max 368 |
| span down           | always 71  | median 57-83, max 148 |
| tallest open column | max 56     | max 117 |

The part that took measuring: **growing the envelope alone does not make a
bigger cave.** The lattice that carves the rooms is a density, so a
double-size box just gets twice as many rooms of the same size — and the
extra space went into cracks the gnome can't fit in (walkable fell 38% to
23%). The lattice, the edge fades and the big chamber all scale with the
envelope now, so a large cave is a scaled-up small one rather than a bigger
box with the same furniture.

Two things I did not smooth over:

1. **Contrast** — how much bigger a chamber is than the passages feeding
   it — misses its bar in canyon: 4.83x against 5.0. The other presets
   make it. That bar came from a population where every cave was the same
   size, so it may simply be the wrong bar now, but I would rather show
   you the gap than move it.
2. **Slightly fewer caves.** 5-6 of 16 worlds have none, against 4-5
   before. A big envelope near a world edge gets shrunk to fit rather than
   thrown away, which recovered most of that but not all.

**Separate question while you are looking:** the broad vertical light and
dark swathes running the full height of both shots. I checked and they are
not from tonight's lighting work — identical with the new glow term and
the old one — so they are either the rock's own regional variation working
as intended, or something nobody has looked at. Is that what you meant by
"pale vertical banding", or was that only the one-pixel formations inside
the cave?
